correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge2\) and real \(q\in(0,1)\), sorting tuples with increasing-label tie-breaking gives a bijection to a permutation and constrained nonnegative gaps; independent geometric series give the exact q-Eulerian PGF. The Savage–Visontai Theorem 5.4 is checked and applies to the same comajor-index polynomial with positive \(q\). Positivity of coefficients and constant one forces all roots strictly negative; PGF normalization yields independent Bernoulli/geometric summands; total nonnegativity follows by Toeplitz products. The standalone path geometric_range_check.py was executed and independently matches 288 exact rational coefficients/normalizations, but is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The general combinatorial factorization in Savage–Visontai (Theorem 5.4) is acknowledged as pre-existing. The specific exact distributional identification for maximum-minus-minimum of fixed-parameter iid geometric data and its Bernoulli-plus-geometric representation and PF-infinity consequence are not asserted in the accessible indexed 2023 order-statistic material or the inspected 2013 polynomial theorem and 2017 random-environment paper; published mathematical comparisons and nine completed semantic database searches found no equivalent or dominating result. Classical P-partitions could indirectly imply the factorization and remain a bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: An exact distributional factorization for sample range, a central statistic of dispersion and joint extreme behavior, upgrades individual-order-statistic shape results to total positivity of every order in a canonical discrete family. The strength is not routine generic closure: a \(\operatorname{Bin}(3,1/2)\) parent is itself PF-infinity but its two-sample range has nonreal-root polynomial (discriminant -15). The explicit Bernoulli/geometric decomposition supplies finite-sample sampling and structural information beyond mean or unimodality.
